before: Gentle meditation or self-hypnosis is a different story. It can really calm your nervous system down, so the guards often ease off on their own, slowly enough for the grown-up in you to keep up. guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
Sometimes There Isn’t a Clear Child Yet

Reparenting assumes there is a coherent inner child to love. For many people, there is. For others—especially people raised in controlling families, rigid religious environments, or any setting where belonging required performing someone else—the authentic child-self may never have had room to form.

The performed self began so early and became so complete that “What do I believe?” or “What do I want?” has no clear private answer. Asking those questions may have been punished, mocked, or made impossible.

Then “love yourself” can feel empty. Love what? The performed self doesn’t feel real, and the authentic self never received the conditions needed to develop. The pl/ork begins earlier, with finding or building the self.

brief:
- reparenting assumes there's a coherent inner child to love; for many people there is
- for others (raised in controlling families, rigid religious settings, or anywhere belonging meant performing someone else) the real child-self may never have had room to form
- the performed self started so early and got so complete that "What do I believe?" or "What do I want?" has no clear private answer; asking those questions may have been punished, mocked, or made impossible
- then "love yourself" can feel empty: love what? the performed self doesn't feel real, and the real self never got what it needed to develop
- so the pl/ork starts earlier, with finding or building the self
